Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Novanet decision criteria & next steps

Thanks again for today's session 

I appreciate you walking us through Novanet's goals and the bake-off plan. Below is a short recap to make sure we're aligned and to capture next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain & goals
- Production latency unpredictability on peak traffic causing user-visible throttling.
- High per-token inference cost at scale; cost is blocking broader rollout.
- Need model consistency across regions (US + EU) with audit logs for compliance.
- Success metric: reduce tail latency >90th percentile by 30% and cut unit inference cost by 25% in production.

Decision criteria (we agreed these matter most)
1) Latency / tail p95-p99 performance under target workloads
2) Cost per 1M tokens at target QPS (forecasted)
3) Deployment flexibility: hosted + private VPC option
4) Observability: token-level cost, per-route dashboards, audit logging
5) Reliability / fallback policies and SLA terms

Competitive comparison (high level) 

- Redwood: strong runtime optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache), private deployment option, rollout tooling. Will present a side-by-side scorecard.
- Competitor A: better initial TCO on small scale but limited private deployment features.
- Competitor B: good EU presence but higher latencies under burst.

Open questions you wanted us to validate during the bake-off
- Realistic end-to-end latency with your peak prompt mix (we'll run a replay test).
- Cost estimates using your token distributions and expected caching benefits.
- Integration tasks for your VPC and KMS 




- any redlines in security checklist?

Proposed follow-ups / tests (from Redwood)
1) Replay test: Redwood will run a 48-hour replay using Novanet's anonymized production traces to measure tail latency and cache hit rates. Deliverable: replay report + p95/p99 numbers.
2) Cost analysis: run cost model using your QPS and token histogram; provide 12-month forecast.
3) Private deployment checklist: share required network/VPN/KMS details; schedule an architecture call with infra (Rishi) to scope effort.
4) Demo + runbook: show failover and A/B rollout with rollback in a canary.

Attachments: scorecard + short summary (attached).

Next steps / owners
- Marissa: send scorecard + schedule replay test kickoff (today)  



ACTION: share replay instructions and S3 location for traces.
- Rishi: schedule architecture call for VPC/KMS (this week).
- Aditya: prepare cost forecast model and initial PO estimate.
- Michael / Asha: share sanitized trace file and confirm legal/security contact for NDA/SC.

Thanks 

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa 


Solid recap, clear and aligned. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Trace file: we'll provide an anonymized replay trace (S3 link) by tomorrow EOD. The trace will contain a ~72-hour window including a heavy traffic spike on Saturday. We can scrub PII but keep timing and prompt distribution intact.
2) Security: our security team will want a short questionnaire answered (SOC2 scope + encryption details). I'll introduce you to our security lead (Lina) in a follow-up.
3) Decision timeline: the exec committee plans to make a final decision by May 10. Key stakeholders beyond Asha and me: product (Michael), infra (Lina), procurement (T. Gomez).

Open question: for the replay test, can you also surface cache-hit behavior at the prompt-prefix level? That will help us estimate how much cold-start vs. hot-prefix access drives costs.

Confirmed: we'll accept the scorecard and the replay test as the primary evaluation artifacts. Looking forward to the replay results.

-Michael
Director, Platform Engineering
Novanet
